test_title: SSC CGL 2022 Tier-I Official Paper (Held On : 09 Dec 2022 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following revolutionaries stated during his trial that “he did not wish to glorify the cult of the bomb and pistol but wanted a revolution in society”?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bhagat Singh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhagat Singh** stated during his trial that** “he did not wish to glorify the cult of the bomb and pistol but wanted a revolution in society”**.
 
• During the **early 20th century Indian independence movement**, Bhagat Singh was a **revolutionary hero**.
 
• He **participated in two well-known attacks on British authority**, one on a local police head and the other on the **Delhi Central Legislative Assembly**.
 
• Bhagat Singh, a fierce critic of British rule in India, was hanged in 1931 at the age of 23 for engaging in activities deemed criminal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Surya Sen**, an Indian revolutionary best **known for organising the 1930 Chittagong Armory Raid**, played a significant role in the **campaign for Indian independence** from British control in India.
 
• A revolutionary from India, **Sachindra Nath Sanyal**, was a **co-founder of the Hindustan Republican Army**, which was **established to engage in military resistance against the British Empire in India**.
 
• A journalist and revolutionary from India, **Barindra Kumar Ghosh **was a **founding member of the revolutionary Jugantar Bengali weekly**.
